answer: Trust is computed, not granted: a small ivory founding set seeds random walks that wander the vouch graph, and a seat's weight is the share of walks that end on it. Clones spend walk mass inside a tight boundary, so per-seat weight falls geometrically as the cluster widens, each member diluting those behind it. To keep k seats above the cutoff, an operator must graft genuine edges into the honest interior, ties that are scarce, personal, and unbuyable in bulk, so the outside ties needed grow faster than k. A lone violet with one true tie keeps its share; a thicket of strangers holds none.
